**Group:** Dinoflagellates  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A distinctive heterotrophic dinoflagellate: a large (often 0.2–2 mm), buoyant, roughly spherical to balloon-shaped naked cell that is mostly transparent with a granular central mass, and has no thecal plates or obvious cingulum. A single striated tentacle and a mouth (cytostome) are used to capture prey, and the flagellum is greatly reduced. Noctiluca scintillans is famous for bioluminescent red tides ('sea sparkle'). Key features: very large size, round translucent balloon shape, feeding tentacle, no girdle.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **gyrodinium** | Other naked dinoflagellates (Gyrodinium, Akashiwo) are far smaller with a clear cingulum; Noctiluca is a large balloon-shaped cell with no obvious girdle and a feeding tentacle. |
| **aggregate** | Aggregates are irregular detrital flocs; Noctiluca is a single large translucent living cell with a rounded outline and central mass. |
